No. `applyDiscount` adds to the existing discount instead of replacing it (`src/cart.ts:18`), so calling `applyDiscount(10)` twice gives 20% off.

Nothing limits the total either. Two calls of `applyDiscount(60)` add up to 120%, and `netTotal()` (line 27) then returns a negative amount. A negative `percent` would raise the price.

If only one discount should ever apply, change line 18 to `this.discountPercent = percent`. If discounts are meant to stack, keep the `+=` but cap the total at 100 and reject negative values.
